00619330.note: The portrait texture builder behind SetPortraitToTexture and SetBagPortraitTexture. Re-read 2026-09-20 after a previous cycle wrongly called it an ordinary texture cache: it is not. On a miss it opens "<path>.blp" itself through FUN_006aff10, pulls the decoded surface with FUN_006af990, swizzles the BGRA bytes, then overwrites every texel ALPHA from a ramp fetched via FUN_006176a0 (+8) -- that ramp is the circular portrait mask -- and creates a fixed 64x64 texture named "Portrait2" via FUN_004b9200, handing it to the region with FUN_00481520 (CSimpleTexture::SetTextureObject, stores at this+0xd4 with an addref/release pair). In front of it sits a name-keyed hash table: FUN_00617c50 looks the path up, FUN_0076f640 hashes it, and the bucket array at DAT_00c5ce74 has a 12-byte stride, built lazily on the DAT_00c5ce7c sentinel. Frozen has none of this, so the two bindings above load the path as an ordinary UI texture instead and are recorded as diverged.

00514ba0.note: Two of its three paths are trivial -- a string argument is returned unchanged via lua_settop(L,1), anything else is nil -- but the number path converts a 1-based button index to a name through FUN_005eec20 and that conversion is unidentified. Frozen's Input::GetButtonName takes a BITMASK (0x1 LeftButton, 0x2 MiddleButton, 0x4 RightButton), so the obvious 1 << (index-1) would make button 2 the middle button, while the Lua convention has button 2 as the right button. 00517020.note: Ported. 0061fec0.note: The tooltip's shared add-a-line helper, and the top unmapped Tooltip.cpp entry in the queue at 204 callers. When the requested line is one past the last, it builds a fresh pair of font strings named "<tooltip>TextLeft<N>" and "<tooltip>TextRight<N>", anchors the left one under the previous line and the right one's RIGHT edge to its own line's LEFT edge, and then it sets the text. Tagging either half would claim a frozen function IS this one when each is half of it, so it stays unlinked. Whoever merges the two halves can link it; the anchor offsets are already recorded in CGTooltipScript.cpp as TOOLTIP_LINE_ANCHOR_Y and TOOLTIP_COLUMN_ANCHOR_X, read from 009e8d00 and 00a0ff3c.

00610a00.note: One gate is skipped. When the unit is the ACTIVE player, the reference requires FUN_006ceb00 -- which is just "DAT_00c9eac8 != 0" -- before reporting the off-hand time, and what sets that global is not identified. It is skipped here. The branch it guards is probably unreachable anyway: it is only reached once the off-hand item has already been confirmed to be item class 2 (weapon), and the server will not let a character equip an off-hand weapon without Dual Wield. Everything else matches: main hand from attackRoundBaseTime[0], off-hand from [1], both unsigned milliseconds scaled by the 0.001f at 009e1134.

0081b530.note: Variadic: it forwards (eventId, format, va_args) straight to the event sink, and it carries BOTH glue events (7 and 8 from the character-list update) and game events (0x15f MINIMAP_PING from the minimap ping store). 00516970.note: Lua handling is ported exactly: argument 1 as a table is resolved with lua_rawgeti(L,1,0) + lua_touserdata + an IsA check against the texture type, and both error strings match the binary. (1) SINK: the reference passes the path to FUN_00619330, which builds a 64x64 alpha-masked portrait texture; frozen calls CSimpleTexture::SetTexture, so the right image appears without the circular mask. (2) BY-NAME FORM: when argument 1 is a string the reference resolves it to a texture through FUN_0048b5f0, a lookup from a global frame name to its object. Frozen has no such registry -- CLayoutFrame::GetLayoutFrameByName returns nullptr unconditionally -- so that form does nothing rather than raising the reference's "Couldn't find texture named '%s'". Two FrameXML callers use it.

005d7180.note: Structure ported from the instruction bytes rather than the decompilation, which lost both the ECX arguments. Order confirmed at 005d71a4-005d7277: resolve argument 1 as the texture (FUN_004a81b0 = FrameScript_GetObjectThis) BEFORE the lua_isnumber check on argument 2; slot-1 rejected below 0 silently and at/above 11 with "Invalid slot in SetBagPortraitTexture"; clear the region (SetTextureObject(0)) before the lookup; ClntObjMgrObjectPtr with mask 4 (TYPE_CONTAINER) from ".\ContainerFrame.cpp" line 1219; icon name via FUN_0070aa00 with the container in ECX; "%s%s%s" of directory, separator and name. Slots 5-11 are the bank bags; the reference already resolves them to a null guid unless the bank is open (FUN_005d6f20 gates indices >= 4 on DAT_00beb9a0/DAT_00beb9a4), so frozen modelling no bank puts those slots on the reference's own away-from-the-bank path and is not counted as a divergence.

0070aa00.note: An item object to its ItemDisplayInfo inventory icon name. DIVERGENCE in route, not in result: the reference dereferences a record pointer the object carries (object+8, then +0xc for the display id) and indexes the table at DAT_00ad3d6c, taking field +0x14. Frozen's CGItem_C holds no such pointer, so it goes entry id -> ItemCacheGet -> displayInfoID -> g_itemDisplayInfoDB and reaches the same row. The observable difference is timing: until the item cache answers for an entry frozen returns an empty name where the reference already has one.

004980d0.note: CORRECTION of the entry added earlier the same day, which called this a driver helper returning "the remaining scale a driver interpolates across" and blocked it as unlinked. That reading was wrong, and what settled it was CSimpleScaleAnim::LoadXML (FUN_0049bd20): the loader validates scaleX and scaleY, clamps them to at least 0.001, and stores 1 - scale. So the object holds the COMPLEMENT, and this function -- {1 - this[0xa4], 1 - this[0xa8]} -- is simply how the scale is read back. It is the getter, not driver arithmetic. DIVERGENCE: frozen stores the scale itself, so its body is a plain copy. The two agree everywhere observable, including at construction, since the reference zeroes the pair and zero is a scale of 1.

00497f30.note: CSimpleAnim::SetSmoothing, the C++ one, and NOT RegisterScriptMethods as the order matcher claimed. Read directly: it takes an ease-in and an ease-out weight, and if either is in (0, 1] it lazily allocates the 12-byte curve object (".\CSimpleAnim.cpp" line 0x30d, vtable 009ebd44) and forwards the pair to the object's own setter. Frozen has no counterpart because it stores the smoothing ENUM and evaluates the curve from that in AnimSmoothingApply, so there is nothing to point at; blocked rather than linked. This address sits inside the run the order matcher filled between AnimSmoothingApply (00497ba0) and CSimpleAnim::Advance (004985f0) -- see the note on that block in docs/ref/parity-animations.md before trusting any link in that range.

00481720.note: A CSimpleTexture getter for the underlying GxTex, and NOT the destructor the order matcher offered. Read directly: it returns TextureGetGxTex(this[0xd4], 1, 0) when the handle is set and 0 otherwise. That +0xd4 is the texture handle is independently confirmed -- it is the same field CSimpleTexture::SetTextureObject (FUN_00481520) writes, found earlier while chasing SetPortraitToTexture. Frozen exposes no such accessor; its callers reach m_texture directly, so there is nothing to point at and this is blocked rather than linked. One of three false links the order matcher produced across 00481620-00481720 once AddAnimTranslation at 00481740 gave it a fresh anchor to fill backwards from; the other two were identifiable and are now tagged.

0053de10.note: GetShapeshiftForm([useUnit]). Traced end to end 2026-09-20 so the next attempt does not have to: the binding reads an optional boolean and hands it to FUN_0053d4b0, which walks the server-sent shapeshift bar DOWNWARD from its count (DAT_00be8e28, entries at DAT_00be8e2c, 8 bytes each with the spell id first), looks each spell up, and asks FUN_00802cb0 whether the player is currently in that spell's form. The result is a ONE-BASED index into the bar, 0 when not shapeshifted, and count+1 for a form that is not on the bar at all. The useUnit argument only gates whether an unshifted player short-circuits to 0. Blocked on two things frozen does not have, and one it now does. It HAS the unit's current form: CGUnit_C::GetShapeshiftForm, byte 3 of UNIT_FIELD_BYTES_2, ported from FUN_0071af70. It does NOT have the shapeshift bar -- no opcode in net/Types.hpp carries it -- and it does NOT have the form field on SpellRec that FUN_00802cb0 compares against. Either alone leaves this unanswerable, so it stays a stub rather than a guess.

0053c0b0.note: GetNumShapeshiftForms. The reference returns the count of entries on the server-sent shapeshift bar (DAT_00be8e28) and nothing else -- the whole body is that global pushed as a number. Frozen registers the shared zero-returner instead, which is correct in the only sense available to it: with no bar received the count really is zero, and FrameXML builds no form buttons. It becomes a real port the moment the bar arrives; see 0053de10 for what that needs.
